usage.scope: Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

external_invariants: Model is ResNetForImageClassification loaded from the local assets directory only (local_files_only=True) in float32; no downloads.
All weights and activations remain FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 are False and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest').
Seed policy: torch.manual_seed(20261020) applied in prepare, matching common.configure().

Input is the real preprocessed image fixture tensor from assets/pixels.npy (3 images, NCHW float32), selected as images[torch.arange(batch) % len(images)].contiguous(); for the frozen 'online' workload batch=1, i.e. the first image, unchanged every repeat.
The model is in eval() mode and the forward pass runs under torch.inference_mode(), identical to the source infer() helper calling model(pixel_values=pixels).logits.
Batch size is fixed at 1 for this workload; the workload, data, precision and output requirements are not altered to improve the score.
Correctness requires all logits within atol=1e-4 / rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 argmax equality against the reference; observations include every logit and the predicted class integer.

Latency is wall time around run() with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, per the source's per-repeat timing; throughput is derived from the unchanged work amount (batch=1) and the measured elapsed time.
The adapter does not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time and never destroys the process group in reset.

selection.rationale: Controlled baseline: largest observed eligible leaf-group CUDA duration, without objective-specific agent selection.
selection.hypothesis: Test whether optimizing this local hotspot improves the complete frozen project objective; local duration is not a predicted project gain.

proposal.rationale: Selection group 5621410346ca09a421d0 covers the three stage-4 aten.conv2d sites (input 1x512x7x7 contiguous, weight 512x512x3x3, padding 1, bias None), 203.0 us of the 727.7 us measured run CUDA time (~28%). Observed per call: cudnn Winograd runs generateWinogradTilesKernel (11.4-11.8 us, filter tiles regenerated on every invocation, i.e. weight-repack work repeated each call) plus scudnn_ampere_scudnn_winograd_128x128 (56.0-56.2 us) launched as 16 CTAs of 256 threads for a 512x49-output problem. Hypothesis (not a measured occupancy fact): 16 CTAs under-fill the ~108-SM Ampere part, so a decomposition exposing more concurrent CTAs should reduce GPU time. Replacement computes the identical FP32 convolution as aten::im2col + one cuBLAS strided-batched SGEMM over K=4608 split into S equal chunks + one deterministic fp32 sum over S partials: K-chunking multiplies GEMM CTA count by S (S=12 -> ~96 CTAs under a 64x64 tiling assumption), removes the per-call Winograd filter transform entirely (weights are consumed through stride views, no packing, no per-call transform), and avoids per-call cudnn plan heuristics. TF32 stays disabled and float32_matmul_precision stays 'highest' because global flags are untouched; mm/bmm therefore run fp32 SGEMM. Output is a fresh contiguous NCHW 1x512x7x7 tensor with the same strides as aten.conv2d, safe under inference_mode and CUDA Graph capture (no host sync, no fixture-dependent caching, no state). Any deviation from the observed shape/stride/dtype/device/bias/scalar signature falls back to the parent operator, so unobserved signatures keep exact parent semantics. CPU verification: max deviation vs fp64 convolution is on the same order as cudnn's own (~1e-6 relative), far inside atol=rtol=1e-4. split_k is exposed because the best chunking depends on the cuBLAS tile choice of the bound GPU and is measured by the search loop; inputs/previous-feedback.txt does not exist, so this is the first attempt with no prior worker feedback to incorporate.

setup_work.build_time_gpu_work: None. build() only reads context metadata and closes over the split factor; no weight transform, no precomputation, no CUDA launches, no allocation, no retained pools or graph-private memory are created at setup. Weights are consumed per call via views (weight.view -> permute with batch stride K/S, row-major lda=4608, cuBLAS-compatible without copy).
setup_work.per_call_transients: im2col columns [4608x49] fp32 (~903 KB) plus split-K partials [S,512,49] fp32 (up to ~3.6 MB at S=36), served by the caching allocator; framework peak_allocated may increase by these transient activations, and this is not a claim of physical-memory savings.
setup_work.state_and_aliases: Stateless replacements; model parameters are never written or re-packed, outputs are freshly allocated, and no alias of inputs or weights is returned.

quality_risks: Summation order changes vs the cudnn Winograd reference (split-K fp32 partial dot products of the 4608-term reduction, then a fixed-order fp32 sum). CPU fp64 comparison shows error of the same magnitude as cudnn's own rounding (~1e-6 relative), but the reference logits are produced by the Winograd path, so this is a genuine numerical difference bounded well inside atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact top-1 unaffected.
Kernels used (im2col, strided-batched SGEMM, sum over dim 0) are deterministic, so repeat-to-repeat outputs are bit-identical and cannot flap the exact_top1 check.

If a torch build decided to materialize the permuted weight view instead of passing lda/strides to cuBLAS, per-call cost would rise (results stay correct); this is a performance risk, not a correctness risk.

Signature-guarded fast path with parent-operator fallback covers unobserved shapes, strides, dtypes, devices, bias, stride/padding/dilation and groups; any fast-path exception also falls back to the parent operator, preserving semantics at the cost of the original kernel.

params.name: split_k
params.description: Number of equal K=4608 chunks in the strided-batched SGEMM replacing each selected conv2d; every choice must divide 4608. split_k=1 is a single mm (cuBLAS picks its own strategy), larger values trade more CTA-level parallelism against a bigger [S,512,49] reduction. Task semantics, batch, sequence length, data and quality thresholds are unchanged for every choice.

constraints.rationale: Equal fp32 K-chunks are required for the batched view; all listed choices already satisfy it and invalid values fall back to the default 12 inside build().
